lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09 the mature search/AutoML frameworks each ship an explicit campaign-management layer, and their primitives converge on the same five things this host hand-rolls. (1) TRIAL LIFECYCLE STATES. Optuna (v5.x stable docs) has exactly five: RUNNING, WAITING (queued but unexecuted), COMPLETE, PRUNED (via TrialPruned), FAIL (uncaught error or NaN objective); unfinished = RUNNING|WAITING. Ray Tune (Ray 2.5x/2.58 docs) tracks CREATING/PENDING/PAUSED/RUNNING/ERROR/TERMINATED with scheduler decisions CONTINUE/PAUSE/STOP returned per result. Ax (Ax 1.0, released Nov 2025; paper Olson et al., AutoML 2025, PMLR v293) has the richest lifecycle: CANDIDATE (still modifiable), STAGED (deployed to an external scheduler, not evaluating), RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED, ABANDONED (user-stopped; data still usable), EARLY_STOPPED (stopped on intermediate data via an EarlyStoppingStrategy). SMAC3 (v2.x) has no user-facing state enum but races challengers against incumbents inside an intensifier with an incumbent trajectory recorded. nevergrad has no states at all - just ask/tell - which is the tell that its campaign layer is the weakest. (2) INCUMBENT PROMOTION RULES. SMAC3 inherits aggressive racing (Hutter et al. 2009): evaluate less-promising challengers on few instances first, gather more evidence only when a challenger might become incumbent; the challenger's budget is adaptively capped at slightly more than the incumbent's total cost (CappedRunException aborts overruns; their own issue #912 records the lesson that 'the maximal runtime cap should never be infinite. If the function never terminates, SMAC will never see any result and wait forever'). irace (Lopez-Ibanez et al. 2016, the direct ancestor of this host's winner gate) eliminates candidates with a statistical race - F-test by default, t-test under capping - after each instance, keeps an elite pool, samples new candidates biased around elites, and the best elite at exhaustion is the incumbent. Optuna's incumbent is implicit: study.best_trial = best COMPLETE trial (feasible-only under constraints), never a RUNNING trial. Ax tracks a best arm via the model posterior and supports challenger-vs-status-quo framing. Ray Tune PBT (Jaderberg et al. 2017) replaces promotion with exploit/explore: a ready trial (every perturbation_interval steps) copies the checkpoint (weights+optimizer+step) of a better trial, then perturbs hyperparams (x1.2/x0.8 continuous, adjacent discrete, or resample at resample_probability=0.25). (3) BUDGET ACCOUNTING. SMAC3's Scenario carries wallclock_limit, per-run cutoff, trial limits (ta_run_limit v1 / n_trials v2), and abort_on_first_run_crash; censored (cutoff-exceeded) runs still count against budget. Optuna counts n_trials and timeout on study.optimize, and MaxTrialsCallback counts only successes. nevergrad has a fixed ask/tell budget with Chaining dividing it across algorithm phases. Ax budgets via total trial counts on the generation strategy. Ray Tune uses per-trial stop dicts plus scheduler time budgets. (4) RESUME-FROM-CHECKPOINT GUARANTEES. Optuna: durable RDB storage keyed by study name; RDBStorage(heartbeat_interval=, grace_period=) plus fail_stale_trials() marks hung/dead trials FAIL and RetryFailedTrialCallback(max_retry) re-queues them - the canonical hung-eval defense; pickled studies cannot cross Optuna versions (use RDB). Ray Tune: experiment state (JSON under storage_path) + per-trial checkpoints; Tuner.restore(path, resume_unfinished=True default, resume_errored, restart_errored); TERMINATED trials are never resumable, and restore is only for ephemeral failures - you cannot change the search space or extend a completed experiment; FailureConfig(max_failures) reschedules trials and whole lost nodes; community-recorded pitfalls include absolute paths baked into experiment state and restore hangs. SMAC3: re-running with the same scenario name/output_directory/seed automatically restores runhistory, incumbent, and model; changed code triggers an explicit resume-or-delete prompt. Ax: AxClient auto-saves the experiment to SQL after each completed trial, and AxClient.load / Scheduler resume from storage. nevergrad: no documented dump/load or resume API (docs silent; GitHub issue #49 is the feature request) [uncertain: whether the current release grew one]. (5) MULTI-FIDELITY RUNG LADDERS. Hyperband (Li et al., JMLR 2017) runs brackets of successive halving at different starting budgets, promoting the top 1/eta per rung with budget x eta per rung (eta=3, R=81 typical), hedging the n-vs-B/n tradeoff; its guarantee is adaptivity, not optimality. ASHA (Li et al., arXiv:1810.05934) makes promotion asynchronous (rung cutoffs from finished trials only) to avoid straggler stalls - Ray's AsyncHyperBandScheduler/ASHAScheduler implements it with time_attr (any monotonic progress measure), max_t, grace_period (minimum fidelity before any stop), reduction_factor (default 4), brackets (softmax-random allocation). BOHB (Falkner, Klein, Hutter, ICML 2018) puts a per-budget TPE/KDE surrogate on top of Hyperband so higher rungs are model-guided; SMAC3's multi-fidelity facade copies the BOHB principle with a random-forest surrogate fit on the highest budget with sufficient observations. Optuna's HyperbandPruner (PFN engineering blog, 2019) is the cautionary design tale: Optuna has no known total budget, so bracket allocation had to be randomized; TPE had to be scoped per bracket via a Study wrapper to keep samplers decoupled from pruners; and the authors state plainly that premature pruning of the eventual best config is unavoidable ('there is no way to prevent this'). Ax's Percentile early stopping terminates a trial whose partial curve falls below a percentile of comparable trials at the same step, with documented safeguards (only after a minimum number of progressions, only against completed-curve baselines); their example run early-stopped 69 of 87 trials for ~71 percent capacity savings. PARALLEL TRIALS: Optuna is shared-storage, no inter-process communication, duplicates possible (constant_liar in TPESampler penalizes running trials to avoid duplicates); SMAC3 parallelizes via a Dask target-algorithm executor or N independent SMAC instances exchanging state through a shared filesystem; Ray Tune splits proposal (searcher) from kill/pause decisions (scheduler) and handles placement; Ax supports BatchTrial for arms that must be evaluated jointly; nevergrad distinguishes batch_mode (synchronous batches of num_workers) from steady-state async. HARD-WAY LESSONS that recur across all five: resume must be built before the crash, not after; hung evals need a bounded cap and a staleness detector; NaN/poisoned objectives must map to a FAIL state, not abort the study (Optuna FAQ: 'trials that return NaN are treated as failures, but they will not abort studies'); first-run crashes need explicit policy (SMAC abort_on_first_run_crash, and their issue #125: a first-run timeout can leave the surrogate with zero data points and crash it - this host's 'degenerate case in the oracle itself' rediscovered); SQLite is 'never' recommended for parallel Optuna (no SELECT...FOR UPDATE, database-locked, NFS failure) and MySQL's case-insensitive collation silently merges parameters a/A; Bayesian guidance degrades at high worker parallelism while random search parallelizes trivially (Ray's analysis found random search roughly 2x as effective as BO with ~10 parallel workers [uncertain: exact provenance of the 2x figure]); PBT needs checkpoint_interval matched to perturbation_interval, hyperparams can drift out of the declared range under perturbation, and the audit trail (pbt_global.txt with target/clone/iteration/old/new config) is treated as mandatory practice.
lacuna.applicability: TRANSFERS TO THE WECO-LOCAL LONG-RANGE RUNNER (resume, timeout, watchdog, lanes, cadence): (a) RESUME - the single biggest gap this host has. vllm_ab_run.py accumulates restarts in memory and appends to ab-ledger.json only at campaign end, so a mid-window death loses the run (the window-3 K-sweep's four arms were exactly this casualty). Optuna's model - durable per-trial records with explicit states, fsync'd after every pair - transfers verbatim at wrapper level: after each interleaved pair, write the trial record (state COMPLETE/FAIL/PRUNED + raw row values + sigma + assertions) to the ledger JSON before starting the next pair, so resume re-reads the ledger, skips finished pairs, and continues the interleave schedule from where the drift-neutralizing A,B,A,B sequence actually stopped. (b) TIMEOUT + WATCHDOG - the hung-eval defense none of the host's runners has: vllm_ab_run.py's subprocess.wait() is unbounded. Adopt SMAC's issue-#912 lesson as a hard rule ('the cap must never be infinite'): per-restart wallclock timeout in the wrapper, kill on overrun, mark the arm FAIL (never silently skip), plus abort-on-consecutive-failure (already present on the probe driver) as the campaign-level backstop. Optuna's heartbeat/grace/requeue triple is the pattern for the supervisor: touch a timestamp per pair, a watchdog marks STALE past grace and re-queues with a bounded retry count (RetryFailedTrialCallback semantics). (c) INCUMBENT QUEUE - Optuna's enqueue_trial/WAITING state is precisely the runbook's 'ordered list staged for the next window': machine-readable pending queue that survives restarts, consumed FIFO, with skip_if_exists to keep operators and agents from double-entering the same probe. (d) BUDGET ACCOUNTING - SMAC's three-axis budget (wallclock_limit + per-run cutoff + trial count) maps one-to-one onto the 72h GPU window: the runner should count spent eval-seconds (the resource that actually runs out) and stop opening a new pair when the remaining budget cannot fund it - the window-4 'closed at ~11h of 72 because all phases delivered' judgment becomes a mechanical rule instead of a judgment call. (e) ADAPTIVE INTENSIFICATION - the gate is fixed-3-pairs today; SMAC's adaptive capping and irace's race say: when |delta| lands inside the gate but above half the gate (the 'borderline' zone this host already hit at gate-0 7/8), escalate pairs (3 -> 5 -> 9 cap) rather than withhold or accept; below half the gate, stop early and bank the GPU time. This is a two-line change to the pair loop. (f) LANE CADENCE - Ax's Client polling loop (get_next_trials -> RUNNING -> complete/abandon with recorded reason) is the shape of a multi-lane coordinator over weco-local sessions: lanes claim work, states live in the shared ledger, ABANDONED-with-reason keeps culled lanes' data usable by later campaigns, EARLY_STOPPED formalizes culling a lane whose partial rows sit below a percentile of comparable lanes at the same fidelity step. (g) PBT EXPLOIT/EXPLORE - maps onto champion-ledger workflow mechanics: exploit = a new lane starts from the champion's committed worktree (warm start, the exact analog of loading a better trial's checkpoint); explore = the mutation ledger's stochastic proposals around the frontier; perturbation_bounds = the legality model already enforcing occupancy/red-lines. PBT's audit-trail discipline (who-copied-whom at which iteration) is already satisfied by lane SHAs + MEMORY entries; formalize it as a ledger column. (h) RUNG LADDERS - this host's kernel-search three-rung ladder (2 M-points x 3 reps -> full M sweep -> adversarial shapes) IS successive halving; what the frameworks add is the bookkeeping: explicit rung tables (budget per rung, per-rung survivor cutoffs), ASHA-style asynchronous promotion (evaluate the next candidate at rung 1 as soon as rung-1 slots free, promote against cutoffs set by finished trials only - no straggler stalls), and grace_period semantics (minimum fidelity before any cull, the analog of 'never gate on fewer than N exactness cases'). DOES NOT TRANSFER, and why: (i) surrogate-guided proposal over CODE DIFFS - TPE/GP/RF models assume a vector-valued, smooth-ish parameter space; a git diff is neither, so Optuna/SMAC/Ax's core value (the model) does not ride the weco-local mutation loop; it already applies where the space IS knob-shaped (engine configs, PPS/K sweeps) and stays there (schedule.py already uses Optuna TPE for exactly this). (ii) MID-TRAINING PRUNING inside one eval - Hyperband's kill-at-rung assumes the expensive thing is divisible training; this host's expensive thing is a full engine restart whose eval is short once up, so the fidelity axis is pairs/reps/shape-rows BETWEEN restarts, not steps inside one; nothing inside a single gate-arm run should be pruned. (iii) PBT WEIGHT-SPACE CROSSTALK - code variants have no interpolable weightspace; exploit copies whole worktrees (git, not checkpoint tensors), so BOHB-style model reuse across rungs of the SAME variant family only. (iv) CENTRAL PARALLEL DEDUP (constant_liar) and BatchTrial arm-weights - the host is single-machine, GPU-serialized; parallelism here is time-interleaved lanes over one device, where the existing pair-interleaving discipline (which the frameworks LACK - they assume stationary, homogeneous evals, while this host measured 9-27 percent cross-restart bands and neutralized them by design) is already stronger than anything in the five frameworks. That is the honest exchange rate: they give resume/timeout/states/budget bookkeeping this host lacks; this host's paired-interleave, noise-floored winner gate, oracle-before-timing, and assertion provenance are primitives they do not have (irace's instance-paired race is the closest ancestor). (j) weco-local specifics: the fork's local mode has no server-side campaign state; 'weco observe' JSONL is the append-only log but carries no trial-state machine, no resume, no watchdog - so all of (a)-(e) land in tools/campaign-runner as a wrapper around the eval binaries, never inside weco [uncertain: whether the fork's weco run gained session resume in 0.4.0; the skill docs do not claim it].

design.mechanism: The campaign-state ledger, implementable cold in tools/campaign-runner as one JSON file plus one supervisor loop. SCHEMA: { 'campaign_id': '<sha of arm specs + model + protocol>', 'champion': { 'label', 'config_digest', 'committed_rows', 'gate_evidence' }, 'queue': [ { 'id', 'arm', 'params', 'state': 'WAITING' } ], 'trials': [ { 'id', 'pair_index', 'arm', 'state': 'RUNNING|COMPLETE|FAIL|PRUNED', 'restart_log', 'rows': {short_decode, ctx512_decode, ctx2048_decode}, 'sigma', 'assertions': {backend, kv_tokens, preempted}, 'heartbeat_ts', 'wall_s', 'exit_code' } ], 'budget': { 'window_open_ts', 'eval_seconds_spent', 'eval_seconds_limit' }, 'rungs': [ { 'fidelity': 'reps|shape_set', 'budget', 'cutoff', 'survivors': [trial_id] } ] }. STATE MACHINE (Optuna's five states, minus PRUNED's mid-eval meaning, plus this host's gates): WAITING -> RUNNING -> COMPLETE (rows parsed, assertions held) | FAIL (exit!=0, timeout, oracle red, NaN metric) ; FAIL -> WAITING at most retry_max=3 times (RetryFailedTrialCallback semantics); heartbeat_ts updated after every engine restart inside a pair; supervisor marks STALE (-> FAIL) when now - heartbeat_ts > grace (600s default). EXIT-CODE CONTRACT from the gate child: 0 = clean, 3 = numeric gate failure, 5 = timeout-killed (wrapper enforces per-restart timeout around subprocess, SIGKILL after grace - the never-infinite-cap rule). WRITE DISCIPLINE: fsync the ledger after every state transition, before the next engine restart begins (Optuna's per-trial durable record); resume = re-read ledger, recompute the interleave position (pair_index parity decides which arm goes next), continue; finished pairs are never rerun. WINNER GATE (unchanged math, adaptive breadth): verdict per row on medians, gate = max(5.0, 300.0 * sigma) as today; escalation rule - if gate/2 < |delta| <= gate, pairs += 2 (cap 9) and re-open the pair loop (irace/SMAC adaptive-capping analog); if |delta| <= gate/2, accept A_WINS/NO_DIFF and stop spending (early stop). BUDGET RULE (SMAC's three axes): the runner refuses to start a new pair when budget.eval_seconds_limit - budget.eval_seconds_spent < max observed pair wallclock; window close = mechanical, not judgment. QUEUE RULE: staged probes from the runbook enter as WAITING entries (enqueue_trial analog) with skip_if_exists on arm+params digest; the coordinator pops only from the queue, so a crashed session's intent survives. RUNG RULE for sweeps: rungs table with per-rung budget and survivor cutoff set by finished trials only (ASHA async promotion); grace = minimum exactness cases before any cull; promotion = top 1/eta (eta=3 default) by gated medians. PBT RULE for lanes: new lane forks champion worktree (exploit) + mutation proposal (explore); ledger records clone source and iteration, the pbt_global.txt analog.
design.failure_modes: Hung evals: frameworks converged on bounded per-run cutoff + heartbeat/grace + bounded retry (Optuna heartbeat_interval/grace_period/fail_stale_trials; Ray FailureConfig(max_failures); SMAC CappedRunException with the recorded 'never infinite cap' lesson); this host currently has an unbounded subprocess.wait() - a wedged NCCL init or JIT build hangs the whole window silently. Poisoned metrics: Optuna maps NaN objectives to FAIL-without-study-abort; SMAC censors timeout runs but still spends budget; this host's defense (oracle before timing, degenerate-case batteries) is stronger at detection, but the ledger has no FAIL state for a poisoned row - a bad row can sit as a quiet median input; the design adds FAIL + retry_max. Silent skips: Optuna without heartbeat leaves RUNNING trials zombie forever; Ray resume breaks on absolute paths in experiment state and on moved checkpoint dirs; SMAC abort_on_first_run_crash=False masks a first-arm crash to a log line; the defense everywhere is explicit state + explicit reason codes, never absence. Drift/nonstationarity: none of the five handles cross-restart variance (they assume homogeneous evals); the host's interleaved pairing is the known defense and must be preserved through resume (resume continues the A,B,A,B parity - a naive resume that finishes all of one arm's pairs first re-opens the drift hole). Parallel/async: duplicated trials in shared-storage Optuna (accepted, constant_liar mitigates), MySQL collation merges a/A parameters, SQLite locks under parallel; BO degrades at high parallelism vs random search; PBT perturbation drifts hyperparams out of declared ranges and its replay does not reproduce checkpoint copies. Premature pruning: Optuna's own Hyperband authors state killing the eventual best config early is unavoidable - the mitigation is grace_period (min fidelity before cull) and brackets; adopt grace as 'no cull below N exactness cases / below 2 reps'.
design.effort_estimate: Wrapper-level (tools/campaign-runner + a thin refactor of vllm_ab_run.py): ledger schema + per-pair fsync + resume + interleave parity (about a day); per-restart timeout + exit-code contract + heartbeat/grace watchdog (half a day); enqueue queue + budget rule (half a day); adaptive pair escalation (two lines in the gate loop). Fork-level: none required for the above; only if weco run sessions must pause/resume mid-flight would the fork change - avoid by keeping weco observe logging and campaign state in the wrapper. Doctrine-only: rung-table bookkeeping and the PBT exploit/explore lane rule are runbook + ledger-column conventions, not code.
design.priority_signal: FOR load-bearing: the 72h windows are the scarcest resource on this host; one mid-window death already cost four K-sweep arms (window 3) and a rerun; every framework older than this project treats durable trial state + hung-eval caps + budget accounting as table stakes because campaigns without them lose work exactly when machines fail; the champion ledger is the host's core asset and making it re-derivable mid-campaign (not just post-hoc) is the difference between a ledger and a log; the escalation rule directly addresses the observed borderline class (gate-0 7/8) where fixed 3 pairs is either too few to trust or too many to waste. AGAINST: this is a single-machine, single-operator setup with campaigns measured in hours, not a fleet - Optuna's RDB/heartbeat machinery, Ray's distributed placement, and Ax's SQL storage are disproportionate; a JSON file with fsync plus a 50-line supervisor delivers the same guarantees here; the surrogate/parallelism machinery that dominates those codebases does not transfer to code-diff search at all. NET: adopt resume/timeout/watchdog/queue/budget (high value, small scope); formalize rung tables and escalation (medium); skip storages, samplers, and distributed schedulers (no lane for them on one TU102 pair).
